title: Scalar adjunction transport between internal and sectionwise module sheaves
statement:
Let $C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe, with abelian sheafification whose local equivalences are monoidal, and its closed symmetric monoidal sheaf tensor [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]. For a commutative ring object $R$ let $R_{\rm sec}$ be its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and let $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\rm sec})$ be the equivalence preserving underlying sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Given a ring-object map $a:R\to S$, write $a_{\rm sec}:R_{\rm sec}\to S_{\rm sec}$ for its section map. Internal restriction and coequalizer extension are those of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; sectionwise restriction and sheafified extension use [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then there are canonical natural identifications
$$E_R\operatorname{Res}_a\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a_{\rm sec}}E_S,\qquad E_S\operatorname{Ext}_a\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{a_{\rm sec}}E_R,$$
with the latter sending the balanced generator $s\otimes m$ to the same generator. They identify the specified extension/restriction adjunctions, including unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ and counit $s\otimes n\mapsto sn$.

On ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] their termwise equivalences identify the K-flat derived scalar extensions [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and exact derived restrictions, including these specified derived adjunctions. On flat-term K-flat representatives the extension comparison is the localization of the displayed termwise map. There is no flatness assumption on $a$.

proof.text: For an internal $S$-module $N$, restriction gives the action $R\otimes N\xrightarrow{a\otimes1}S\otimes N\to N$. Under the section reconstruction equivalence this acts by $r\cdot n=a_U(r)n$ over every $U$. This is exactly sectionwise restriction. Both functors leave the underlying sheaf and every morphism unchanged; therefore their identity components give a natural identification $E_R\operatorname{Res}_a\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a_{\rm sec}}E_S$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; sectionwise action calculation for scalar restriction

proof.text: Regard $S$ as an internal $R$-module using $a$. Apply [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] to the two $R$-modules $S$ and $M$. The underlying relative tensor of the internal scalar extension is the coequalizer of the relations $(s\,a(r))\otimes m=s\otimes(rm)$, by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The cited comparison identifies this with the sheafification of $U\mapsto S_{\rm sec}(U)\otimes_{R_{\rm sec}(U)}E_R(M)(U)$ and sends $s\otimes m$ to the same pure tensor. Its $S$-linearity follows from $t(s\otimes m)=(ts)\otimes m$ on both sides; the inverse comparison satisfies the same equation. Thus it is an isomorphism of $S_{\rm sec}$-module sheaves $E_S\operatorname{Ext}_a(M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{a_{\rm sec}}E_R(M)$. Naturality follows because the map induced by $h:M\to M'$ sends $s\otimes m$ to $s\otimes h(m)$ on both sides. These checks on pure tensors determine the sheaf morphisms by the balanced-bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal].

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property following Tag 0GMW

proof.text: For an $S$-linear $f:S\otimes_RM\to N$, its adjoint is $m\mapsto f(1\otimes m)$. Conversely, an $R$-linear $g:M\to\operatorname{Res}_aN$ gives $s\otimes m\mapsto s\,g(m)$: it is balanced since $s\,a(r)g(m)=s\,g(rm)$. The coequalizer and sheaf tensor universal properties make these morphisms, and $f(s\otimes m)=s f(1\otimes m)$ and $1g(m)=g(m)$ prove the formulas inverse. The comparisons in steps 1 and 2 leave these formulas unchanged, so they identify the specified Hom adjunctions. In particular the identity on the extension transposes to $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, and the identity on the restriction transposes to $s\otimes n\mapsto sn$. This identifies the units and counits, with their naturality, rather than merely asserting that two left adjoints are isomorphic.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; explicit scalar-adjunction transpose

proof.text: For $T=R,S$, [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] states that $E_T$ is exact, identifies direct-sum total tensor complexes, and preserves and reflects flat objects, acyclicity and K-flatness. Exactness implies that the termwise equivalence and its inverse carry quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Localizing these two functors and their inverse natural isomorphisms gives mutually inverse equivalences of the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Step 1 holds termwise and hence after localization. Internal scalar restriction is exact by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], so its derived functor is termwise restriction; its sectionwise counterpart is exact as well, since step 1 conjugates it by exact equivalences. This proves the required comparison of exact derived restrictions.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; passage to localization is the explicit agent argument

proof.text: For a complex $K$ of internal $R$-modules, apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the ringed site $(C,R_{\rm sec})$ to $E_RK$. Pull the resulting flat-term K-flat resolution back along $E_R$; step 4 makes it a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P\to K$. The site and universe hypotheses in the statement are exactly those needed for these module sheaves and their sheafification. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], sectionwise scalar extension on these representatives inverts quasi-isomorphisms and computes its universal left derived functor. The termwise comparison of step 2 therefore implies the same inversion property internally. Conjugating the sectionwise universal left derived pair by the derived equivalences of step 4 gives the universal left derived pair for internal extension: its factorization property is unchanged under equivalences. This is the K-flat derived scalar extension denoted in [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Its comparison at $K$ is represented by the chain isomorphism $E_S(S\otimes_RP)\cong S_{\rm sec}\otimes_{R_{\rm sec}}E_RP$ of step 2. The canonical independence of the K-flat resolution in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes this natural in the derived object. Thus on the flat-term K-flat representatives required in the statement it is exactly the localization of the displayed termwise map. No tensor functor on arbitrary complexes is claimed to preserve quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, specialized to the identity topos with ring map a_sec

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-hom-comparison] to the sheafified extension and exact restriction for $a_{\rm sec}$, with the ordinary adjunction of step 3 and the universal left derived pair of step 5. Its normalized transpose formula determines the specified derived adjunction. More explicitly, for $q:P\to K$ as in step 5 the derived unit is represented by $K\xleftarrow{q}P\to\operatorname{Res}_a(S\otimes_RP)$, whose second arrow is $p\mapsto1\otimes p$. For an $S$-complex $N$ choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P\to\operatorname{Res}_aN$; the derived counit is represented by $S\otimes_RP\to N$, $s\otimes p\mapsto s\,q(p)$. These are the normalized transposes of the identity morphisms: after the invertible derived comparison at $P$, the cited formula reduces them respectively to the ordinary unit and the ordinary transpose of $q$. Steps 1--3 and 5 identify each of these chain maps and each resolution arrow with its sectionwise version. Thus the derived comparisons identify both specified derived units and counits, hence the adjunctions. This argument uses neither flatness of $a$ nor preservation of K-flatness by scalar restriction.
